Subject: Governed MPA reanchor and acceptance sprint

Emily — attaching the latest MPA (v0.3) and a short proposal for a concentrated final-mile sprint to protect the go-live window. Key asks in this message:

- Review the updated acceptance checklist (section 3) — we tightened criteria to remove ambiguity around performance baselines.
- Confirm whether Neptune wants the canary plan (2-day parallel runs) or the fast-swap approach; both are budgeted below.
- If the two eval tests your team flagged can't be completed by 4/23, we need a re-baseline proposal and a decision on a small one-time service credit to keep momentum.

Attachment: Neptune_MAP_v0.3.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync today if helpful.

— Laura

Laura / team — thanks for the update and the clear checklist. Quick status from our side: two automated evaluation tests (load and tokenization edge-case) slipped after last night's run; dev lead expects them completed by COB Monday (4/19), not Friday. That pushes our internal acceptance gate and risks the 4/30 rollout.

We have three asks:
1) Can Redwood run the canary with reduced scope on 4/22 so we at least exercise the rollback and metrics?
2) What is the one-time credit you can offer if final acceptance moves beyond 4/30 due to these test delays?
3) Procurement wants a clean MAP annex with explicit PO acceptance criteria (they asked to be CC'd).

Attachment: Neptune_eval_summary.xlsx (summary of failing test cases)

– Emily

Emily — appreciate the heads-up. Short plan from sales/solutions to keep the go-live intact:

- Canary partial run on 4/22: Redwood will execute the canary limited to the two integration points (load + tokenization). We'll provide the full telemetry and a rollback runbook.
- Credit: we can offer a one-time service credit equal to 5% of the first-month usage invoice if acceptance slips past 4/30 due to Neptune-side test delays. This is a one-off goodwill credit tied to test-completion dates in the MAP annex.
- Re-baseline proposal: see the attached CSV for three scenarios (A: on-time, B: 1 week slip, C: 2 week slip) with proposed acceptance windows and impact to invoicing.

Action items for Neptune: confirm canary scope for 4/22 and indicate whether Procurement will accept the MAP annex language. If Procurement prefers a PO amendment instead of annex language, we can route a DocuSign amendment (link to follow).

Attachment: proposed_rebaseline.csv

— Ben

Vivek — forwarding the thread. Quick summary and request for exec sign-off:

- Situation: Neptune dev delays (load/tokenization) are likely to move acceptance beyond 4/30 unless partial canary on 4/22 gives us confidence.
- Proposed remediation: run partial canary on 4/22 (ops-runbook ready), offer a capped 5% one-time credit if acceptance slips > 4/30, and include a MAP annex stating acceptance criteria and credit trigger.
- Commercial impact: small revenue deferral if credit triggers; reputational benefit if we keep partnership momentum.

Asking for: approval to commit the 5% credit and to send a DocuSign annex to Procurement. If approved, Ben will issue the DocuSign link and I will coordinate with Legal for final language.
